sections.h2: What does selling a house in Tyler, TX involve?
sections.html:
Selling in Tyler means choosing between a retail listing, a private sale and a direct purchase by a cash buyer, then clearing whatever sits between you and a clean closing: a mortgage payoff, tax balance, tenant or estate paperwork. The route that fits depends on how quickly you must move and how much work the house needs.

Start by pulling together the loan payoff figure, the latest property tax statement and any letters about liens, code issues or foreclosure. Those papers tell you what a closing would have to pay off and whether anything has a deadline attached.

  • Retail listing: the most exposure, with showings, inspections and lender timelines to absorb.
  • Private sale: you control price and terms and carry the paperwork yourself.
  • Direct cash purchase: fewer conditions and a closing date set to your calendar, with the offer adjusted for repairs.

sections.h2: Where is Tyler and how did the city take shape?
sections.html:
Tyler is the Smith County seat, ninety-nine miles southeast of Dallas, and the Handbook of Texas lists U.S. highways 69 and 271 plus State highways 14, 31, 64, 110 and 155 among its routes. The legislature authorized the townsite in April 1846, and the city was named in honor of President John Tyler.

Commissioners paid $150 in February 1847 for a 100-acre tract and laid out twenty-eight blocks around a central square. Tyler was incorporated on January 29, 1850. Railroad machine shops arrived in the late 1870s and 1880s, and the city's population nearly tripled between 1880 and 1890.

Census figures give the modern footprint: 57.45 square miles of land and roughly 1,845 residents per square mile in 2020. Older streets around the square and newer subdivisions farther out mean house ages in Tyler vary a lot, so expect an inspector to focus on whatever systems date the house.

sections.h2: Which industries have shaped Tyler's housing demand?
sections.html:
Oil, roses, health care and education each left a mark. The 1930 East Texas oilfield discovery drew oil companies and field developers to Tyler, and the population climbed past 25,000 by 1933, according to the Handbook of Texas.

Rose growing was the other signature business. By the 1940s, more than half of the rose bushes sold in the country were raised within ten miles of the city, which is why the Texas Rose Festival is held each October. The same entry lists the University of Texas Health Center at Tyler, Mother Frances Hospital, Texas College, Tyler Junior College and the University of Texas at Tyler.

Those institutions bring steady job and campus traffic. Census figures show 2022 retail sales near $4.84 billion and health care and social assistance receipts around $3.47 billion, far ahead of accommodation and food services at about $617 million.

sections.h2: How does Tyler compare on Census housing measures?
sections.html:
Tyler's typical owner-occupied house is valued at $235,300 in the 2020-2024 Census estimates, and 55.4 percent of housing units are lived in by their owners. Individual houses vary widely around that midpoint.

About 85.7 percent of residents were in the same house a year earlier, and median household income is $67,486. People moving to Tyler therefore tend to be fewer than those staying, which keeps the buyer pool tied to jobs and campuses.

sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax on a Tyler house?
sections.html:
The Smith County Appraisal District values the property and processes exemptions, while the Smith County Tax Office bills and collects. The tax office stresses that it has nothing to do with valuations and that the appraisal district is not part of county government, so value disputes go to the district at 903-510-8600.

The tax office, at 903-590-2920, accepts payment in person, online, by mail to P.O. Box 2011, Tyler, Texas 75710, or at a drop box. Card payments carry a 2.30 percent fee with a $1.50 minimum, and electronic checks carry none. Substations in Noonday and Lindale also take property tax payments.

The county's printed schedule for unpaid current-year tax shows these totals for penalty and interest:

  • February 7 percent, March 9, April 11, May 13 and June 15.
  • July 18 percent plus a 15 percent collection fee, then 19 in August and 20 in September.
  • Interest then continues at one percent a month, and taxes unpaid by June 30 go to the delinquent tax attorney.

sections.h2: What should a Tyler seller know about appraisal rules and exemptions?
sections.html:
The appraisal district's FAQ explains that a homestead's taxable value can rise no more than 110 percent of the prior year's value, and that a buyer claiming the exemption for the first time gets no cap that year. Owners 65 or older get a ceiling on school taxes that can rise if they add a room, pool or garage.

Your protest deadline is printed on the notice of appraised value, and the review board may excuse a miss only for good cause such as a medical emergency. If you appeal while a case is pending, you still pay the lesser of the undisputed tax or the tax under the order being appealed.

State law also gives school districts a $140,000 homestead exemption. When you sell after January 1, ask your title company how the buyer's exemption claim will be handled for the remainder of that year.

sections.h2: What if the Tyler house is inherited, tenant-occupied or in foreclosure?
sections.html:
Each of these has its own paperwork and clock. For an inherited house, offering a will for probate generally has a four-year window, and a muniment of title can pass title when only real-estate liens exist. A transfer on death deed must have been recorded before the owner died.

For a house with a tenant, written notice to vacate is at least three days unless the lease says otherwise, and the suit is filed in justice court. For a mortgage in default, the borrower has 20 days after the default notice to catch up, and the sale notice must come at least 21 days ahead of an auction held on a first Tuesday.

Deeds go to the Smith County Clerk, so ask that office for current recording costs.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Tyler appraisal?
faqs.a: Call the Smith County Appraisal District at 903-510-8600. The Smith County Tax Office does not handle valuations and says so on its own page.

faqs.q: Where can I pay Tyler property tax?
faqs.a: The Smith County Tax Office takes payment in person, online, by mail and at a drop box, and substations in Noonday and Lindale also accept property tax. Card payments carry a convenience fee, while electronic checks do not.

faqs.q: What happens if Tyler taxes go unpaid after January 31?
faqs.a: The county's schedule adds penalty and interest starting at 7 percent in February, rising monthly. After June 30, unpaid tax is referred to the delinquent tax attorney and a collection fee applies.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Tyler house while a parent's estate is still open?
faqs.a: Usually only with proper authority. A personal representative can sign after appointment, or a muniment of title or recorded transfer on death deed may apply. A title company will tell you which papers it needs.

faqs.q: Is a cash offer worth considering for a Tyler house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: It can be, because the buyer takes the house as it stands and prices the work in. Compare the offer with what a listing would net after repairs, fees and carrying costs.
